variants.title: Separate the planes
variants.context: The control plane handles identity, title availability, manifests, and policy; the media plane delivers high-bandwidth segments close to viewers. Pressing Play fetches a menu of renditions and repeatedly asks a nearby cache for the next few seconds.
variants.prompt: Which decision belongs to the control plane?
options: Whether an entitled member may receive a time-limited playback manifest.
optionFeedback: Identity, availability, manifests, and policy are control-plane work.
variants.explanation: Control decisions and Open Connect delivery are separate.

variants.title: Separate the planes
variants.context: The control plane handles identity, title availability, manifests, and policy; the media plane delivers high-bandwidth segments close to viewers. Pressing Play fetches a menu of renditions and repeatedly asks a nearby cache for the next few seconds.
variants.prompt: A control-plane outage occurs mid-playback. What should happen to a stream already playing?
options: It should continue from the nearby cache within its budgets; the manifest was already issued.
optionFeedback: A control-plane problem should not stop segment delivery.
Segments come from the media plane.
Players fetch segments, not whole files.
variants.hint: Which plane is the player talking to now?
variants.explanation: A control-plane problem may change the experience but must not become an origin stampede.

variants.title: Separate the planes
variants.context: The control plane handles identity, title availability, manifests, and policy; the media plane delivers high-bandwidth segments close to viewers. Pressing Play fetches a menu of renditions and repeatedly asks a nearby cache for the next few seconds.
variants.prompt: Why is average bandwidth insufficient proof of a healthy stream?
options: The player needs enough throughput over time to refill its buffer, and the fleet needs reserve for spikes and miss bursts.
optionFeedback: Continuity depends on buffer refill, not the mean.
Bandwidth matters; the average is the wrong statistic.
variants.hint: What does a viewer feel that an average hides?
variants.explanation: Measure startup, rebuffering, quality, and origin protection.

variants.title: Prepare the package
variants.context: Ingest converts a source into a publishable package: validate the source, encode a rendition ladder, package and verify aligned segments and manifests, then publish immutable outputs before the catalog advertises availability.
variants.prompt: A studio delivers a new title. Put the ingest steps in order.

items.text: Validate integrity, duration, tracks, rights window, and metadata under a stable asset identity.
Encode a rendition ladder across bitrates, resolutions, and codecs.
Package aligned segments and manifests; verify timing, captions, audio, and protection metadata.
Publish immutable versioned outputs, expose them to caches, and only then advertise availability.

variants.explanation: Publish must be atomic from the viewer’s perspective.

variants.title: Prepare the package
variants.context: Ingest converts a source into a publishable package: validate the source, encode a rendition ladder, package and verify aligned segments and manifests, then publish immutable outputs before the catalog advertises availability.
variants.prompt: A re-encode fixes a caption bug. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Keep the same asset identity so the retry does not create a competing package.
Re-package and re-verify alignment and captions.
Publish a new package version; update catalog availability afterwards.

variants.hint: Stable asset identity prevents competing packages.
variants.explanation: Versioned outputs let old and new packages coexist safely.

variants.title: Prepare the package
variants.context: Ingest converts a source into a publishable package: validate the source, encode a rendition ladder, package and verify aligned segments and manifests, then publish immutable outputs before the catalog advertises availability.
variants.prompt: A title is scheduled for a regional launch. Put the steps in order.

items.text: The source is validated and rights-windowed for the region.
Outputs are distributed to caches, then catalog availability opens in that region.

variants.hint: Caches are filled before the catalog opens.
variants.explanation: Catalog availability owns whether a profile in a region may start a package.

variants.title: Budget the delivery
variants.context: One viewer at a rendition consumes a continuous bitrate and requests discrete segments. Lower hit rates push bytes and requests to the origin; shorter segments raise request rates.
variants.prompt: One million concurrent viewers at 5 Mbit/s. How many Tbit/s of edge bandwidth?
variants.explanation: 1,000,000 × 5 Mbit/s = 5,000,000 Mbit/s = 5 Tbit/s at the edge.

mistakes.feedback: One million times five megabits is five terabits.

variants.title: Budget the delivery
variants.context: One viewer at a rendition consumes a continuous bitrate and requests discrete segments. Lower hit rates push bytes and requests to the origin; shorter segments raise request rates.
variants.prompt: Edge bandwidth is 5 Tbit/s and the cache hit rate is 95%. How many Gbit/s reach the origin?
variants.hint: Multiply by the miss rate and convert.
variants.explanation: 5 Tbit/s × 0.05 = 0.25 Tbit/s = 250 Gbit/s at the origin.

variants.title: Budget the delivery
variants.context: One viewer at a rendition consumes a continuous bitrate and requests discrete segments. Lower hit rates push bytes and requests to the origin; shorter segments raise request rates.
variants.prompt: One million viewers each request a new segment every 4 seconds. How many segment requests per second?
variants.explanation: 1,000,000 ÷ 4 = 250,000 requests per second; shorter segments raise this rate.

mistakes.feedback: Divide by the segment duration, do not multiply.
Each viewer requests one segment per four seconds.

variants.title: Adapt the stream
variants.context: Adapt to measured throughput, buffer level, and decoder limits. Prefer uninterrupted lower quality over a repeated pause. Average bandwidth is not proof of a healthy stream.
variants.prompt: Throughput drops below the current rendition’s bitrate. What should the player do?
options: Step down to a sustainable rendition; uninterrupted lower quality beats a pause.
Keep the quality and pause to buffer.
variants.hint: Which failure hurts the viewer more?
variants.explanation: Prefer uninterrupted lower quality over a repeated pause.

variants.title: Adapt the stream
variants.context: Adapt to measured throughput, buffer level, and decoder limits. Prefer uninterrupted lower quality over a repeated pause. Average bandwidth is not proof of a healthy stream.
variants.prompt: Shorter segments are proposed for faster adaptation. What is the trade-off?
options: More requests per second and manifest overhead, which makes miss storms harder to absorb.
optionFeedback: Request rate rises with shorter segments.
variants.hint: What happens to requests per second?
variants.explanation: Segment duration trades adaptation speed for request pressure.

variants.title: Adapt the stream
variants.context: Adapt to measured throughput, buffer level, and decoder limits. Prefer uninterrupted lower quality over a repeated pause. Average bandwidth is not proof of a healthy stream.
variants.prompt: Which signals should drive the rendition choice?
options: Measured throughput, device capability, buffer level, and decoder limits.
optionFeedback: Advertised speed is not measured throughput.
Tiers may cap quality but do not replace measurement.
variants.hint: What can the player actually observe?
variants.explanation: Adapt bitrate and resolution to measured conditions.

variants.title: Keep the records apart
variants.context: Keep three records separate: the source asset, the playback package, and catalog availability. A manifest must never advertise segment URLs that have not passed validation and distribution gates.
variants.prompt: A manifest lists segments that failed validation. What rule was broken?
options: Publish must be atomic: manifests must not advertise segments that have not passed validation and distribution gates.

variants.title: Keep the records apart
variants.context: Keep three records separate: the source asset, the playback package, and catalog availability. A manifest must never advertise segment URLs that have not passed validation and distribution gates.
variants.prompt: Which record decides whether a profile in a region may start a title?
optionFeedback: The package is the versioned output.
variants.hint: Which record is region- and profile-aware?

variants.title: Keep the records apart
variants.context: Keep three records separate: the source asset, the playback package, and catalog availability. A manifest must never advertise segment URLs that have not passed validation and distribution gates.
variants.prompt: Is the source asset used to deliver segments?
options: No. Segments come from the versioned playback package; the source is validated studio input.
optionFeedback: The source is not a segment-delivery object.
variants.explanation: The playback package owns rendition IDs, segment maps, and checksums.
